claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing/fiscal-year revenue (Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time).
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion as of Q2 2026.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
The 2026 predictions in last year's edition of this piece held up (it predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade).
Gartner stated that by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027, and described cloud as becoming a business necessity by 2028.

McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings, EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations, and Asia leads projected cloud value followed by the US and Europe.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS reported $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's AI business and chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) are growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Microsoft Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026 (ended June 30, 2026), up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026, and backlog rose from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
ResearchAndMarkets says hybrid cloud will grow from $130B to $310–330B by 2030.
Mordor Intelligence says 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers found 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one cloud.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending (software, hardware, services) to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% year-over-year increase.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.
Enterprises are investing in GPU provisioning and orchestration, data pipelines, vector databases, feature stores, and LLM infrastructure.
Pulumi Policies can help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates using AI.

Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications, with total spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney said AI doesn't deliver value on its own and needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance.
Gartner states that by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% are running a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: 'Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects ... cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications.'
Large tech companies are the first adopters of platform engineering and Internal Developer Platforms, and mid-size to large companies continue to invest in them.

Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.

In Pulumi's 2026 survey, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes, yet manual approval remains close to universal today; Pulumi's report describes this as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rise from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
CNCF's report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, a decline the report attributes to the technology's growing maturity.

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, with Kubernetes often used as the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration across edge and core.
Pulumi published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools at /blog/best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026/.
AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams.

Gartner says that by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Pulumi released Pulumi Agent Skills, which teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server that gives AI assistants infrastructure access, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The post frames trends as shaping 2027, with AI agents moving from writing code to operating infrastructure with humans approving changes.
